newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares close lower before long weekend.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares close lower before long weekend.

text.p: The Bel-20 index of leading shares ended slightly down on Thursday with investors unwilling to take positions on first day of new two-week account ahead of long weekend during which key U.S. jobs data announced, and shortly before U.S. elections.
The Bel-20 index shed 0.20 percent, or 3.64 points to 1,795.03 with a modest 1.2 billion francs worth of Belgian shares traded.
"Volume's lousy and it's a three day weekend with U.S. elections 48 hours after that," one dealer said, noting foreign gold shares were amongst the most heavily traded stocks.
"Buyers have been absent all week," another dealer said.

Friday's U.S. October unemployement figures, expected to be unchanged at 5.2 percent, should give further indications as to whether the Federal Reserve will feel inclined to raise short term interest rates at its mid-November FOMC policy meeting.
Bank BBL was among the leading losers, slipping 2.0 pct to 6,420 francs.

Traders said they were becoming more negative for financial stocks as a whole and were starting to shift to cyclicals, fearing that the Bank of England rate rise was the start of an upward trend in Europe.
One notable stock was was utility holding Tractebel, which edged up 0.2 percent to 14.850.

The subject of a 14,500 francs a share public bid by holding SGB, Tractebel has been the subject of market interest for several weeks as small retail clients took profits and professionals bought for the put warrant which SGB is offering to dissuade shareholders from actually taking up the offer.

The put warrant allows shareholders to sell Tractebel stock at 14,500 francs in three years' time. SGB had been obliged to make the public offer, which ended on Wednesday, after buying a stake in Tractebel from holding GBL.
SGB's parent Suez said in a Belgian newspaper that in fact SGB had not bought a single share in the public offer.
